goals: Mechanistic: estimate long-term mean vertical drainage/recharge flux (QDRAI) leaving the ELM soil column as a function of soil texture and forcing variability
Validation: constrain the recharge estimate indirectly via water-table depth (WTD), since no recharge observations exist in-domain
key_processes: water partitioning (ET vs drainage vs runoff)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the vertical water balance and produces a column-base drainage flux that is the best available proxy for potential recharge; spatial sampling spans the watershed's soil heterogeneity.
model_choice.coupling_note: The 'true deep water table' recharge with lateral groundwater redistribution requires ELM QDRAI -> PFLOTRAN transient recharge BC. That coupler is not implemented; standalone ELM gives potential (column-base) recharge only. Listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: Soil-texture control on column-base drainage (potential recharge) flux
Interannual / multi-year variability of potential recharge over 1980-2018 as a long-term mean after spin-up
Spatial pattern of potential recharge across dominant soil classes

not_answerable.aspect: True steady-state recharge reaching the DEEP regional water table
not_answerable.why: Standalone ELM has no lateral groundwater flow and a simplified/free-drainage bottom boundary; it cannot route the column flux to a regional deep aquifer.

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation/snow-driven control on recharge (the dominant control across 352-1977 m)
not_answerable.why: Framework lacks elevation-downscaled forcing; columns run under uniform forcing show soil variation, not the elevation/snowpack recharge signal.

not_answerable.aspect: Direct validation of the recharge magnitude

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 dominant soil classes are the only VALIDLY-forced driver; crossing them with 3 elevation bands (used as spatial-context/placement, not as a forced climate axis) gives 12 exploratory columns to span the recharge-relevant heterogeneity the stack can actually represent. Elevation bands are kept for placement and later coupled work, NOT presented as isolating an elevation/snow effect.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in valley-bottom / lowland zones where deep recharge to the regional aquifer is most plausible and where USGS wells exist; distribute remaining columns across mid and upland bands to characterize soil-driven drainage differences.
sampling_strategy.replication: None beyond the soil x band cross; N kept minimal because forcing is uniform and additional replication would not add an independently-forced signal.

sampling_plan.reason: Highest potential deep-recharge zone; coarse soils maximize drainage and this is where wells allow WTD checks.
Contrasts drainage against coarse soils in the same recharge-relevant lowland where validation data exist.
Spans the soil-texture range at intermediate elevation to characterize soil control on column-base drainage.
Captures thin/coarse upland soils and their drainage behavior; flagged that snow-driven recharge here is not properly forced.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — match columns to well locations where they fall within a sampled soil/elevation group
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density in-domain

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — compare modeled WTD pattern against the gridded prior as a spatial sanity check, not a point measurement
GAP — no recharge measurements; only indirectly constrained via WTD. Could pursue analog-site process validation if an external recharge dataset is ingested.

experiment_summary.validation: subset of the 12 that co-locate with USGS wells (data-dependent)
experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline forcing (1980-2018 multi-year mean after spin-up), native gridded soil per column

requires_capabilities.capability: ELM->PFLOTRAN one-way coupling (QDRAI -> transient recharge BC)
requires_capabilities.why: Route column-base flux to a laterally-connected deep aquifer
requires_capabilities.blocks: Answering 'true deep water table recharge' as posed

requires_capabilities.why: Represent the elevation/snowpack control on recharge across 352-1977 m
requires_capabilities.blocks: Isolating the dominant elevation/snow driver of recharge

requires_capabilities.why: Report a long-term mean/steady recharge rather than transient

requires_capabilities.blocks: Any co-located validation of the recharge estimate

requires_capabilities.why: Assign soil class per column from real rasters
Assign elevation band and place valley-bottom columns

assumptions: ELM QDRAI (sub-surface drainage) is the accepted proxy for potential recharge in the standalone (uncoupled) design.
Elevation bands are used for placement/context only; under uniform forcing they do NOT isolate an elevation-driven recharge signal.
A long-term mean over 1980-2018 after spin-up approximates 'steady-state' for reporting purposes.
Dominant soil classes will be resolved by the downstream expander from gridded soil rasters.
open_questions: How many USGS wells actually fall within the Naches domain, and at what depths (deep vs perched)?
Is any external/regional recharge estimate (e.g. USGS SIR, water-balance product) acceptable as an analog constraint given no in-domain recharge data?
Is building the ELM->PFLOTRAN coupler in scope, or should this be scoped as potential-recharge only for now?
Should we prioritize investing in elevation-downscaled forcing given it is the dominant recharge control here?
